title: Quantitative Analytics and Model Expert - GenAI Governance
description: Position Overview At PNC, our people are our greatest differentiator and competitive advantage in the markets we serve. We are all united in delivering the best experience for our customers. We work together each day to foster an inclusive workplace culture where all of our employees feel respected, valued and have an opportunity to contribute to the company’s success. As a Quantitative Analytics and Model Expert within PNC's Model Risk Management organization, you will be based in Pittsburgh, PA / Tysons Corner, VA / New York City. This opportunity is focused on GenAI governance, ensuring generative AI solutions align with regulatory requirements, organizational policies, and risk management standards. PNC is an in-office company that fosters a supportive culture where employees can thrive and achieve balance. We encourage candidates to connect with their recruiter and hiring manager to understand workplace expectations and ensure the role aligns with their goals. PNC will not provide sponsorship for employment visas or participate in STEM OPT for this position. Job Description Provides strategic and analytical insights around quantitative analyses, processes, and validations. Reviews complex quantitative analyses and models and engages with the Line of Business to enhance model development by incorporating business feedback. Oversees the development of new model frameworks by supporting the line of business and provides consultative feedback around improvements. Reviews any recommended changes to existing models. Conducts executive level communication during the course of the review. Performs the most complex qualitative and quantitative assessments on all aspects of models including theoretical aspects, model design and implementation as well as data quality and integrity. Reviews reports and associated quantitative analysis and provides analytical insight into potential areas of improvement. Reviews validation of existing models and assesses model risks. Reviews the evaluations of identified model risks and provides high level consultation around recommended conclusions on strengths and limitations of the model. Provides consultative feedback around the preparation and analysis of regulatory compliance documents. PNC Employees take pride in our reputation and to continue building upon that we expect our employees to be: Customer Focused - Knowledgeable of the values and practices that align customer needs and satisfaction as primary considerations in all business decisions and able to leverage that information in creating customized customer solutions. Managing Risk - Assessing and effectively managing all of the risks associated with their business objectives and activities to ensure they adhere to and support PNC's Enterprise Risk Management Framework. Qualifications Successful candidates must demonstrate appropriate knowledge, skills, and abilities for a role. Listed below are skills, competencies, work experience, education, and required certifications/licensures needed to be successful in this position. Competencies Bank Quantitative Analysis, Consulting, Data Gathering and Reporting, Effective Communications, Predictive Analytics, Quantitative Techniques, Regulatory Environment - Financial Services, Testing Work Experience Roles at this level typically require a university / college degree. Higher level education such as a Masters degree, or PhD is desirable. Industry experience is typically 8 + years. Specific certifications are often required. In lieu of a degree, a comparable combination of education, job specific certification(s), and experience (including military service) may be considered. Education Bachelors Certifications No Required Certification(s) Licenses No Required License(s) Language Assessments No Required or Preferred Language Assessments Pay Transparency Base Salary: $133,000.00 – $296,400.00 Salaries may vary based on geographic location, market data and on individual skills, experience, and education. This role is incentive eligible with the payment based upon company, business and/or individual performance. Application Window Generally, this opening is expected to be posted for two business days from 10/19/2026, although it may be longer with business discretion. Benefits PNC offers a comprehensive range of benefits to help meet your needs now and in the future. Depending on your eligibility, options for full-time employees include: medical/prescription drug coverage (with a Health Savings Account feature), dental and vision options; employee and spouse/child life insurance; short and long-term disability protection; 401(k) with PNC match, pension and stock purchase plans; dependent care reimbursement account; back-up child/elder care; adoption, surrogacy, and doula reimbursement; educational assistance, including select programs fully paid; a robust wellness program with financial incentives. title: Policy Program Manager, Safeguards Regulatory
description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As a Program Manager on Anthropic's Safeguards team, you'll help make sure we meet our obligations under AI safety laws and regulations around the world. Working closely with Legal, you'll turn new and emerging requirements into programs, controls, and deliverables. This requires a detailed understanding of how our models and products are built, evaluated and safeguarded. Your work will support Anthropic's commitment to developing AI safely and beneficially as the regulatory landscape evolves. The responsibilities listed below are some examples of areas that someone in this role could own, depending on their experience and the team's needs. Key responsibilities Manage and drive complex safety initiatives that identify, assess and mitigate risks from frontier models, from initial risk assessment through to the deployment of safeguards Partner with the Safeguards incident management team to strengthen incident response and reporting processes, including the policies that determine how incidents are escalated and when they must be reported externally Conduct post-incident reviews, and work with the subject matter experts for each harm area to incorporate the findings into model and product safeguards Own the safety strategy and deliverables for AI systems used in high-risk settings, including risk assessments, technical documentation, and the information that deploying customers need to use those systems safely Define the safety and risk controls that our models and products require, ensure that each control has an owner and a documented procedure, and confirm that it operates as intended Partner closely with the owners of each risk area to develop a deep understanding of AI risks, safety evaluations and mitigation strategies, and use that understanding to prepare safety documentation, transparency reports and regulatory submissions Minimum qualifications Experience in trust and safety, AI safety or a related field, including designing and implementing safeguards against misuse or harm Understanding of AI safety, including the principal risk areas and the evaluations and safeguards used to address them, well enough to engage substantively with the technical experts responsible for them Experience running risk assessment or harm mitigation programs from identification through to resolution Experience translating policy or regulatory requirements into practical operational processes Ability to drive complex, cross-functional programs to completion in a fast-moving environment, including with technical teams outside your own discipline Clear written communication, including documentation for technical, legal and external audiences Strong attention to detail, and the judgment to recognize when work is at risk and raise it early Commitment to the safe development and deployment of AI Preferred qualifications Experience with AI-specific regulation, such as the EU AI Act Experience leading incident response programs, including escalation paths and external reporting obligations Experience preparing safety documentation, transparency reports or regulatory submissions Experience working with technical and research teams on safety evaluations The annual compensation range for title: Counsel
description: About Public Public is the world’s first agentic brokerage, combining a comprehensive multi-asset investing experience with all the advantages of AI Agents. Members can invest in stocks, options, bonds, crypto, and event contracts, and manage a variety of accounts including their personal brokerage, margin, retirement accounts, and business accounts—all in the same place. Since 2019, Public has raised $400 million. Investors include Accel, Tiger Global, Will Smith's Dreamers VC, The Chainsmokers' Mantis VC, as well as renowned figures in business and culture, like Maria Sharapova, Tony Hawk, and NYU Stern professor Scott Galloway. About the role We’re looking for a sharp, enthusiastic attorney to join our Legal team. This is a generalist role with an emphasis on litigation, regulatory matters, compliance, privacy, and product counseling. You will also help expand our AI governance program.  Public is a highly regulated financial services and technology company. Experience in a regulated financial field is a plus, but this role would also suit a strong generalist who is willing to climb the regulatory learning curve. This role is based in New York City, and you’ll work from our office Monday through Thursday. What you’ll do You’ll handle a little bit of everything, including: Litigation, investigations, and exams. You’ll manage disputes from start to finish, including escalated customer complaints, FINRA arbitrations, privacy claims, and civil litigation, handling many matters yourself and overseeing outside counsel on others. On the regulatory side, you’ll respond to inquiries and investigations, partner with Compliance on examinations, and help turn lessons learned into better products and processes. Broker-dealer, investment adviser, and prediction markets regulation. Public owns an SEC-registered investment adviser and a FINRA-member broker-dealer that is also a CFTC-registered futures commission merchant. You’ll partner with Compliance on our SEC, FINRA, CFTC, and NFA obligations, including AML, regulatory filings, and registrations. You’ll also monitor regulatory developments, help keep our policies and procedures current, and translate complex rules into practical advice and training for our business teams. AI governance. You’ll work on the program that governs both our customer-facing AI products and the AI tools our teams use internally. That includes setting practical policies and quality assurance processes, assessing new AI use cases, and tracking emerging laws and guidance. Privacy and cybersecurity. You’ll own our privacy program, from privacy notices and consumer requests to data mapping and record retention. You’ll also partner with Engineering and IT on cybersecurity, fraud prevention, and incident response, including any resulting customer remediation. Product counseling. Regulations shape every part of our business, from the customer-facing product to back-end operations. You’ll work closely with our Product, Engineering, and Marketing teams from concept through launch, spotting risks early and finding practical ways to navigate those rules.  Contract negotiation. You’ll help draft, review, and negotiate a wide range of commercial agreements, including vendor, marketing, and data agreements. Legal processes and systems. You’ll build playbooks and templates that help our business teams navigate legal and compliance requirements and negotiate the best deals possible. You’ll also keep improving the tools, systems, and processes our team relies on, using AI to make our work faster and more efficient. Qualifications J.D. from an ABA-approved law school (or foreign equivalent) Admission to at least one U.S. bar, in good standing 2-5 years of legal experience, ideally at a top law firm and then in-house at a technology or financial services company / start-up Experience with a broad range of legal matters Strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate cross-functionally and influence senior stakeholders A high level of integrity and the ability to balance legal and compliance obligations with business objectives Comfort with ambiguity and pressure, and the ability to identify, prioritize, and resolve issues quickly and independently A track record of quickly learning and using new software, such as project management and compliance tools Experience using AI tools responsibly to make legal processes and systems more efficient, or a demonstrated willingness to learn Bonus points Experience with any of the following: Litigation, arbitration (especially FINRA), or regulatory examinations and investigations Broker-dealer, investment adviser, or futures regulation Privacy, cybersecurity, or AI governance programs Negotiating commercial agreements, such as vendor, marketing, and market data agreements Partnering with compliance teams to build efficient, effective compliance systems and processes Compensation The base salary range for this role is $120,000 to $170,0

We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion. Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. ABOUT THE ROLE: We are looking for an experienced attorney to join our Commercial Counsel team. This senior role will help build and support Notion’s rapidly evolving Enterprise customer sales motions, bringing deep expertise in negotiating complex AI SaaS agreements with enterprise customers, as well as acting as an advisor and coach to our account teams and cross functional partners. Notion is scaling rapidly, and we need people who work well as a tight-knit team with a passion for driving revenue deals to conclusion. If you enjoy using your deep industry and technology transaction expertise to support revenue generating functions, this role is for you. Our Commercial Legal team sits at the center of Notion’s growth. We simplify how customers contract with us, take clear and unambiguous positions on AI, privacy, and security, and drive revenue deals to a fast, predictable close. That means exercising real judgment and finding creative, pragmatic paths forward through complex customer requests and requirements. This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE: - Have broad responsibility for negotiating SaaS AI agreements and providing practical day-to-day commercial legal support - primarily in the Americas region - for the sales, marketing, channels, and customer success teams with a focus on supporting the Enterprise segment - Collaborate with Product Legal team on product and operational items that impact customer agreements and go-to-market initiatives - Draft and negotiate complex agreements regarding privacy, security, and AI regulatory matters - Identify and independently pursue process improvements for buy-side supporting motions - Develop and revise contract templates and playbooks as necessary, based on changes in our product offerings, organization, and law SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING: - Admitted to the California State Bar, New York State Bar, or Registered In-House Counsel in good standing - 10+ years of combined experience practicing as a commercial attorney within a law firm or software technology company - 2+ years in-house experience at a SaaS and/or AI technology company - Privacy and artificial intelligence subject matter expertise, including privacy regulations (GDPR, e-Privacy Directive, CCPA, etc.) and AI regulations (EU AI Act) with the ability to incorporate evolving requirements into the customer facing agreements - Experience driving commercial transactions, SaaS, and enterprise B2B transactions - Strong negotiation skills, including ability to explain nuanced legal concepts to internal and external parties and tailor approach to the audience - Excellent drafting, written and verbal communication skills and ability to adapt legal requirements in balanced, creative and pragmatic ways to facilitate communication at all levels of the organization - Ability to directly interact and build meaningful relationships and trust with internal and external clients and leaders - Demonstrated curiosity about AI and a willingness to adopt AI tools to work smarter, move faster, and deliver better results.
